title: Beauty Shop
full_review:
First, there was the Chicago-set "Barbershop." Then "Barbershop 2: Back in Business." Both had Ice Cube and a male-dominant perspective. And now the latter film's Gina Norris is back in action, this time in Atlanta, with basically the same formula, but from the distaff side.

As embodied by the estimable Queen Latifah, "Beauty Shop" (MGM) finds the single mom working as a hairdresser to support her little girl, Vanessa, a budding classical pianist for whom Gina resolutely wants to have the best.

After a falling-out with her boss, flamboyant Jorge (scene-stealing Kevin Bacon with a blonde perm), Gina quits and decides to open her own establishment.

Getting financial help from the bank proves difficult, but after demonstrating her beautifying dexterity to an officer there, she succeeds in securing a small loan. It's only enough to take over a dilapidated beauty parlor in the ghetto, along with its disgruntled, laid-back staff.

Two of the workers -- disdaining Gina's new no-nonsense policies -- walk out on her, but the others are willing to give her new management a try. Gina even hires the smart and sweet but definitely white-bread stylist, Lynn (Alicia Silverstone), her buddy from Jorge's shop, to join her despite initial skepticism from the neighborhood staffers (including Alfre Woodard, Golden Brooks and Sherri Shepherd).

Gina spruces the place up, and even though the wiring is on its last legs, she's able to make do, with the help of the good-looking, piano-playing electrician (Djimon Hounsou) who lives just above the shop, and to whom little Vanessa -- and later Gina herself -- takes a shine.

Before long, Gina's white society customers (Andie MacDowell and Mena Suvari) from Jorge's seek her out for her special know-how and especially her magical hair conditioner.

But, besides the faulty wiring and a devastating vandalism incident, Gina must also contend with a mean-spirited -- and corrupt -- city inspector who's ready to fine her for any infractions.

You just know that, ultimately, thanks to her styling prowess and warm-hearted people skills Gina will overcome any and all obstacles.

Bille Woodruff's engaging film is a perfect showcase for the likable Latifah, who also served as one of the producers.

The eclectic ensemble cast, including Della Reese, Bryce Wilson, Sheryl Underwood and Keshia Knight Pulliam, not all of them generally known for comedy, makes for interesting watching.

Despite some salty language -- even from a streetwise youngster -- and salon sex chatter, overall "Beauty Shop" imparts solid messages about loyalty, friendship and parenting.

This film contains some profanity, crude language and crass expressions, sexual innuendo and suggestive dancing. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
